topics.title: Systems of classification in the plant kingdom

concepts.learning_objective: Distinguish artificial systems such as that of Linnaeus from natural systems such as that of Bentham and Hooker.
Explain that phylogenetic systems are based on evolutionary relationships and assume a common ancestor for members of a taxon.
Identify numerical taxonomy, cytotaxonomy and chemotaxonomy as aids to classification.
Describe algae as chlorophyll-bearing, simple, thalloid, autotrophic, largely aquatic organisms of varied form.
Distinguish vegetative, asexual and sexual reproduction in algae, including isogamy, anisogamy and oogamy.
State the ecological and commercial uses of algae such as agar, algin, carrageen and Chlorella.

topics.title: Classes of algae: Chlorophyceae, Phaeophyceae and Rhodophyceae

concepts.learning_objective: Describe the pigments, stored food, cell wall and flagella of green algae.
Describe the pigments, stored food, body organisation and reproduction of brown algae.
Describe the pigments, stored food, habitat and reproduction of red algae.
Explain why bryophytes are called amphibians of the plant kingdom and state their ecological importance.
Explain the dominant haploid gametophyte and the dependent diploid sporophyte of bryophytes.
Compare the plant body and reproduction of liverworts and mosses, including gemmae and protonema.
Describe the dominant vascular sporophyte and the free-living prothallus of pteridophytes.
Explain heterospory and why it is regarded as a precursor to the seed habit.
Classify pteridophytes into Psilopsida, Lycopsida, Sphenopsida and Pteropsida with examples.
Describe the roots, stems and leaves of gymnosperms and their adaptations.
Explain heterospory, strobili, the reduced gametophytes and the formation of naked seeds in gymnosperms.
State the defining features, range of size and classes of angiosperms.
Distinguish gymnosperms from angiosperms on the basis of ovules and seeds.
